seriesName: AWS p5e.48xlarge EC2 Capacity Block rate through 2026's quarterly hikes

points.label: After January 2026 hike (~15%, most US regions)

notes: All three bare numbers are quoted from a single GPUSmith article (published 2026-07-26) that traces the p5e.48xlarge EC2 Capacity Block instance-hour rate through AWS's January 2026 and July 2026 quarterly price hikes. This instance type (p5e, H100-class) is not the same one named in today's bullet (B300, which GPUSmith only gives a single July 2026 figure for: $112.32/instance-hour = $14.04/accelerator-hour, matching the bullet's pre-October baseline), but it is published by the same site and shows the same quarter-over-quarter upward pattern the bullet describes. The October 2026 figure itself (the bullet's actual subject) is not yet published on this page -- GPUSmith's piece predates the October 7 hike and only notes AWS's pricing page says prices are 'scheduled to be updated next in October, 2026.' Treat this chart as context for the pricing-hike pattern, not direct confirmation of the October number in the bullet.
